messages.author: fe756cf51e487a56
messages.subject: returning an HTTP error code?
parts:
Hi, I am running RApache under Apache 2.0, 64 bit linux with R 2.10. I
have an r-script handling requests. At the end of the function that is
called I do

return(DONE)

but at one point I need to return a HTTP_BAD_REQUEST. But when I add

return(HTTP_BAD_REQUEST)

to the code I get an error response:

Apache Warning/Error!!!<br><br>ParsedFile(/home/guhar/public_html/r/
tester.R) failed!

How does one return status codes other than DONE & OK?

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: returning an HTTP error code?
parts:
Do you have ROutputErrors configured in your httpd.conf? This turns error messages into HTML, which is probably not what you want.

I'm not sure what exactly your intention is, but I usually don't use any return value at all. The default handler will return 200 if your code runs OK, and it will return 500 if an error pops up.

return(HTTP_BAD_REQUEST) works fine for me, but only if no other code is printed before that. So you have to manually buffer your output until you know for sure that you want to return a 200 OK, and nothing else.

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: returning an HTTP error code?
parts:
Yes,

This situation comes up when developers use sys.source with r-script like so:

<Directory /var/www/R-files>
SetHandler r-script
RHandler sys.source
</Directory>

When a request comes in for a file within that directory, it is
equivalent to calling sys.source() with that file as an argument. The
downside is that you cannot use the return() statement with
sys.source(). The only way to return a correct value is to make it the
last expression in that file.

If one were to use brew instead, then one can use return().

Jeff
